title: Redwood Discovery - Model selection + deployment options - Pelagic Robotics
summary: Intro discovery focused on model selection for multimodal marine robotics assistant; discussed hosted vs dedicated vs private deployments, context length needs (80k+ tokens for mission logs), multilingual support (EN, ES, PT), and tool-calling for telemetry and mission control. Customer requested cost/latency tradeoffs, security docs (SOC2, KMS), and a small pilot / benchmark on their dataset.
topics: open model comparisons (Llama variants, Mistral, Mixtral)
context length and KV cache implications
tool-calling / function calling for mission control
action_items: Jordan Lee - Send preliminary pricing and dedicated capacity options (due: 2027-01-04)
Maya Patel - Share model comparatives doc and recommended quantization profiles (due: 2027-01-05)
Dr. Elena Ortiz - Provide sample mission logs and telemetry schema for benchmark (due: 2027-01-06)
next_steps: Redwood to share pricing + security pack (SOC2, ISO summary, KMS integration notes)
Customer to upload 1 week of anonymized mission logs to s3/prescribed link for benchmarking
Schedule technical POC kickoff (1hr) week of 2027-01-11 with SE-led benchmark
transcript:
14:00:02 Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining - I'm Jordan with Redwood. quick round robin?
14:00:10 Dr. Elena Ortiz: Hi, Elena here, head of ML at Pelagic. we run models for mapping and mission planning.
14:00:18 Samir Khan: Samir, CTO. I'll be listening for infra/security questions.
14:00:22 Priya Iyer: Priya, product. happy to capture requirements.
14:00:28 Jordan Lee: Great. Maya, Carlos from SE team are on - Maya will talk model tradeoffs. Maya?
14:00:34 Maya Patel: Hi all, thanks. quick context check: you mentioned long mission transcripts and multimodal telemetry, is current average sequence length like 20k tokens or more?
14:00:45 Dr. Elena Ortiz: yeah, for long missions we often see 40k to 80k token equivalents once we concatenate sensor text, operator transcripts and annotations. some missions exceed that.
14:00:55 Maya Patel: ok, that's super helpful. so we should be thinking about extended context models or chunking with strong KV cache.
14:01:05 Samir Khan: also need multilingual - english and spanish and some portuguese. and tool-calling - the model needs to call a mission-control API to trigger waypoints.
14:01:17 Carlos Nguyen: when you say tool-calling, do you mean structured function calls / tool invocation? or just suggested actions?
14:01:24 Samir Khan: structured. we need deterministic calls: sample, create_waypoint({lat,lon,eta}), plus telemetry queries.
14:01:33 Maya Patel: cool, long context + tool-calling steers us to evaluating models that support function calling primitives and large context windows. open models that have multi-k context: Mistral Mixtral derivatives, Llama 3 variants with up to 128k, and some commercial ones.
14:01:46 Priya Iyer: what's the gap between Hosted and Dedicated for this use?
14:01:52 Jordan Lee: good question. Hosted is fastest to integrate and we manage everything - best for time-to-value. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and predictable throughput, lower jitter, and isolation for data. Private (VPC/on-prem) is for when you need full network isolation or regulatory control.
14:02:08 Dr. Elena Ortiz: we have regulatory concerns around telemetry PII and vendor access. likely need Private or Dedicated with strict KMS.
14:02:17 Maya Patel: from model perspective, Dedicated lets you pin quantized model variants and tune kernels for 80k contexts more reliably. Hosted can run larger models too but with shared capacity and potentially more variability.
14:02:29 Samir Khan: how about latency? for mission control calls we need sub-second for small prompts, but longer analyses can tolerate seconds.
14:02:38 Carlos Nguyen: so typical tradeoff: larger context and bigger models increase latency and cost. we can propose hybrid patterns: local lightweight model for control plane + Redwood hosted/dedicated for heavy analysis.
14:02:55 Dr. Elena Ortiz: interesting - could you show numbers or an estimate?
14:03:00 Maya Patel: rough numbers: a 70B-family quantized model on a dedicated GPU pool can hit ~150-300ms p50 for short prompts; 3-5s for 80k context extracts depending on batching. hosted will be a bit higher variance. cost scales with token compute - batching and KV cache help.
14:03:20 Priya Iyer: Open-source model choice - are there recommendations for multilingual performance?
14:03:26 Maya Patel: mixtral and llama-family have decent multilingual coverage; Mistral mixtrals tuned for tasks, Llama 3 variants show better few-shot across languages. we recommend running an eval on your Spanish/Portuguese prompts.
14:03:40 Samir Khan: any constraints around function calling with open models? like structured output and safety?
14:03:46 Carlos Nguyen: it's less standardized than APIs like OpenAI's function call but we provide a tool-calling abstraction in the Redwood runtime that can map model responses into structured calls via templates and small verification steps. for mission-critical ops we'd add a validation layer to avoid unintended calls.
14:04:05 Dr. Elena Ortiz: what about tokenization and cost for multilingual? portuguese seems to chew tokens differently in some encoders.
14:04:12 Maya Patel: yes tokenization varies; we include tokenization profiles per model in our catalog so you can estimate token counts per language. helps with cost planning.
14:04:22 Priya Iyer: SOC 2 and key management - requirement for us.
14:04:26 Jordan Lee: we have SOC 2, ISO summaries in the security pack. Dedicated and Private support KMS/HSM integrations; Private gives you customer-managed KMS. we'll share docs.
14:04:38 Samir Khan: good. and audit logs for every call?
14:04:41 Jordan Lee: yes, full audit trails and token-level cost breakdowns in Redwood Console.
14:04:47 Dr. Elena Ortiz: curious about benchmarking - can you run our mission logs and return metrics: latency, token cost, hallucination rate on a test prompt set?
14:04:58 Maya Patel: absolutely. typical POC: ingest sample logs, run across 2-3 model variants (e.g., Llama-3-70B-128k-q, Mixtral-8x7B-80k-q, Mistral-instruct variant), capture latency, cost, and a custom accuracy/hallucination metric you define.
14:05:15 Priya Iyer: what about quantization options? we need to run on cheaper infra if possible.
14:05:19 Maya Patel: we support int8/int4 profiles. dedicated lets you run aggressive quantization plus kernel-selection; Private gives you full control to deploy quantized artifacts on your infra.
14:05:30 Samir Khan: any red flags on hallucination when using KV cache or chunking?
14:05:35 Carlos Nguyen: chunking can create context boundary issues; KV cache preserves prefix state which helps for continuity, but care must be taken on retrieval and prompt stitching. part of the benchmark is measuring those regressions.
14:05:48 Dr. Elena Ortiz: timeline? we'd like to pilot in Q1.
14:05:52 Jordan Lee: sounds good. typical path: quick POC (2-4 weeks) - ingest data, run bench, iterate. can be Dedicated pilot if you want reserved capacity, or Hosted to move faster.
14:06:03 Priya Iyer: cost expectations for a small pilot?
14:06:06 Jordan Lee: we'll send a ballpark - depends on model choice and tokens processed. estimate in the email.
14:06:12 Samir Khan: stakeholder question: who needs to sign off on security? our compliance lead will review SOC2 and network diagrams.
14:06:20 Jordan Lee: we'll include security pack and a suggested network architecture for private/VPC setups.
14:06:26 Dr. Elena Ortiz: okay quick deeper technical: Maya, can you explain how Redwood handles tool-calling mapping when model outputs are noisy?
14:06:34 Maya Patel: yes. we do a 2-step: 1) parsing templates + schema enforcement, 2) a verification policy that checks semantic constraints (e.g., lat/lon range, ETA sanity). we also support a dry-run mode where calls are staged and require operator approval.
14:06:52 Priya Iyer: do you have examples of mission-control integrations?
14:06:56 Carlos Nguyen: we have reference adapters for REST and gRPC, plus event hooks. we can demo a sample create_waypoint flow in the POC.
14:07:05 Samir Khan: any rate limits or throughput caps? we need bursts during simultaneous operations.
14:07:11 Jordan Lee: Dedicated supports configurable autoscaling policies and burst capacity; we can size a GPU pool for your peaks. Private can be sized by your infra team.
14:07:20 Dr. Elena Ortiz: for long context, do you recommend a single 128k model, or a combination of retrieval + model?
14:07:27 Maya Patel: retrieval + model is often cost-efficient: use a small retrieval layer to surface relevant chunks, then feed the model with reduced context. but for some end-to-end tasks a large context model simplifies flow. tradeoffs: latency, cost, and engineering complexity.
14:07:41 Priya Iyer: any known compatibility issues with Mistral-based models and your runtime?
14:07:45 Carlos Nguyen: generally supported; edge cases are ops around attention optimizations. our runtime has kernel-selection per model family; we'll run an onboarding test.
14:07:55 Dr. Elena Ortiz: ok, let's recap next steps.
14:08:00 Jordan Lee: recap: Redwood to share pricing + security pack and model comparatives; Maya to run benchmark once Elena provides sample logs; schedule POC kickoff week of Jan 11.
14:08:12 Priya Iyer: thanks.
14:08:14 Samir Khan: thanks - excited to see numbers.
14:08:18 Dr. Elena Ortiz: thanks all.
14:08:25 [meeting ends]
